chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) permitted the camel herders, when they came at night, to throw (the pebbles).
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for pilgrims who arrive late at night during the stoning of the Jamarah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Prophetic principle of *rukhas* (concessions) in Hajj rituals, specifically accommodating the practical difficulties of camel herders who arrived at the Jamarat at night. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that the stoning is not strictly bound to dismounting when necessity or haste dictates, reflecting the flexibility of Sharia in balancing ritual precision with human circumstance.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww permitted for the camel herders when they came over at night, that they can pelt (the Jamarah)’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who has said the following:

“Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, gave permission to camel attending people to come during the night and throw pebbles.”’
